_comment: An EXAMPLE store pack — the shape the cloud sends this box (EDGE_PACK_FILE).
Every top-level section is optional, and leaving one out is meaningful:
the box then tells the screens it has NOT BEEN TOLD that section, which is
different from telling them the section is empty. The manager's day close
refuses the first and proceeds on the second.
Contains no real store data, no prices anybody trades on and no secrets.
deliveries/drivers/routingPolicy: the box PLANS the routes itself from these,
so vans still go out when the internet is down. `route` overrides the planner
when a dispatcher writes one by hand, and the driver's screen says which it is.
Distances are straight-line: there is no map here, so the plan is a draft.
purchaseOrders/receipts/supplierInvoices/buyingPolicy: the buyer's screen.
Leave buyingPolicy out and the box serves the buyer's screen nothing at all,
because a screen inventing its own match tolerances would be deciding how big
a price difference is worth nobody's attention. The buyer must NOT appear in
approvers: nobody signs off their own capture (roadmap section 28).
categories/productMaster/priceEntries/pricingPolicy: the product and price screen.
Leave pricingPolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a screen
inventing its own margin floor would be deciding how much of the shop's profit is
worth nobody's attention. The person who sets prices must NOT be in approvers.
A product with no unitCostMinor has NO entry in the cost map served to that screen
- not a zero. Zero cost reports a 100% margin, which is a lie that reads as good news.
shelfLocations/shelfAssignments/shelfPolicy: where things sit (M04-FR-02).
This is what puts the picker's list in the order they walk the shop, and every
field is a NUMBER because 'A10' sorts before 'A9' as text and the picker then
walks the aisle twice without ever knowing why. zoneOrder is YOUR cold-chain
decision - leave it out and the walk is ordered by position only, and every
screen says so rather than implying a cold chain nobody asked for.
planogram/shelfCounts/backstock/assortment/spaceAreas/displayContracts: merchandising.
Leave merchandisingPolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a
screen inventing its own refill level would be deciding when a shelf is empty
enough to be worth walking to. A facing with NO count in shelfCounts is reported
as 'never counted' - it is NOT treated as empty, which would raise the loudest
alarm the system has for every product in the shop on day one.
reportingRecords/roles/roleAssignments/reportingPolicy: the reporting screen (D13).
reportingRecords is what this shop ACTUALLY records today, and the gaps are the
point: a report whose fact is not in this list REFUSES BY NAME rather than running
and coming back as zero, because a zero is read as 'nothing happened' and an empty
report is read as 'nothing to worry about'. Leave reportingPolicy out and the box
serves that screen nothing, because a screen inventing its own staleness thresholds
would be deciding, on its own authority, how old a number may be before somebody
should stop making decisions on it. roles/roleAssignments are the shop's OWN access
control, so the same default-deny check that guards an action guards its export.
returnHistory/serviceCases/satisfaction/slaPolicy/servicePolicy: the service desk.
Leave servicePolicy out and the box serves that screen nothing, because a screen
inventing its own return window would be deciding how long this shop takes goods
back for, and inventing its own refund threshold would be deciding how much money
may leave without a second signature. returnHistory is the returns the CLOUD knows
about - another branch's, or ones taken before this box was installed. It is MERGED
with the box's own return log, never replaced by it: the cloud alone leaves the
at-most-once guard blind exactly when the line is down, which is when a shop is
least supervised. THE FIVE NUMBERS IN servicePolicy ARE YOURS TO SET before go-live
- the ones here are starting figures, not a recommendation.
batches/recalls/expiryPolicy: the expiry and recall screen (M10).
PRODUCT taxBps AND status ARE NOW REQUIRED FOR A PRODUCT TO REACH A TILL. Without
a tax rate every line of tax on that sale would be invented, and without a status
the lane cannot tell active from discontinued - so the product is EXCLUDED from the
till catalogue and named in excludedProducts rather than shipped at a guessed rate.
recallBlock STOPS THE SALE AT EVERY TILL, INCLUDING WITH THE INTERNET DOWN. It is
read from here AND from productMaster.recallBlocked, and either one saying blocked
means blocked - a safety flag must fail one way only. A recalled product is shipped
to the lane WITH its block rather than excluded, so the till refuses it by name;
'unknown barcode' on a recalled tin is a cashier keying it in by hand.
Leave batches out and the screen says THIS SHOP RECORDS NO BATCH DATES, which is a
different thing from nothing going out of date - only one of those is good news.
tallyPostings/financeLedger/periodState/financePolicy: the finance screen (M23).
EVERY CONTROL TOTAL IS STATED TWICE AND THE TWO SIDES MUST BE INDEPENDENT.
financeLedger is what YOUR OWN RECORD says the shop took; tallyPostings is what the
ACCOUNTS actually received. Only a posting in state 'posted' counts as received - a
queued one is money Tally has never seen and a dead_lettered one is money it refused.
Counting either would make both sides the same number computed twice, and the month
would close, reconciled and signed, with the accounts empty.
Leave financeLedger out and the screen has NO totals at all - not an empty list, which
would reconcile vacuously - and refuses to close the month by name.
journalPrefixes ARE YOUR CHART OF ACCOUNTS. A heading guessed here would file your
takings where your accountant does not look for them; a posting matching none of them
is raised as 'postings nobody can classify' rather than quietly left out.
accounts/supportSessions/devices/versionPolicy/auditRecords/retentionPolicies/
legalHolds/adminPolicy: the admin and security screen (M01/M02/M33/M34).
SUPPORT ACCESS IS TIME-BOUND AND SCOPED, NEVER STANDING. A grant names exactly what
may be seen - an empty scope list is REFUSED, not treated as everything - and its
expiry is judged from the clock every time the screen is read, never from a stored
flag somebody has to turn off. supportSessions is NEVER PRUNED: somebody outside the
business saw this tenant's live data and that record is the only evidence of it.
Leave versionPolicy out and the screen says NOTHING IS BEING ENFORCED on any device,
which is not the same as every device being up to date. Leave retentionPolicies
empty and it says NOTHING HAS BEEN DECIDED, which is not the same as nothing being
due for deletion. A legal hold outranks a retention date, and nothing deletes.
killSwitches/agentBudgets/aiUsage/aiPending/aiEvaluations/aiPolicy:
the AI control screen (M32/M36/A01-A10).
THE KILL SWITCH IS THE POINT. Leave killSwitches out and the screen says it has NOT
BEEN TOLD - it does not draw ten assistants running, which is what an invented empty
list would do while one of them is actually stopped. A switch is NEVER PRUNED and
never expires by itself: lifting one is a separate, named act by a DIFFERENT person,
because a switch that turns itself off at midnight turns a known-bad assistant back
on while nobody is watching.
AN ASSISTANT WITH NO ROW IN agentBudgets HAS NO CEILING, AND CANNOT MAKE A CALL AT
ALL. That is deliberate: a missing ceiling is not an unlimited one. Leave
platformCeilingMinor out of aiPolicy and the screen shows NO spend summary rather
than reporting every assistant comfortably inside a limit nobody agreed - the
figure here is the owner platform runtime ceiling (decision D3), in paise.
aiPending is what an assistant has DRAFTED. Nothing in it has happened. It happens
when a named person accepts it, and the record names the PERSON as the actor and the
assistant as the drafter - no assistant commits a price, payment, refund, purchase,
stock or privilege change, and no setting anywhere can grant it one.
aiUsage IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF WHAT AN ASSISTANT HAS SPENT, and every entry carries its own
period. There was briefly a second - a carried map of per-agent totals with no period on it -
and on a box that had been running for a month the two disagreed by an entire budget: the
assistants tab read 95,000 spent while the cost tab beside it read nought. Leave aiUsage out
and the screen says the spend is NOT KNOWN and no assistant may make a request, because a
ceiling can only be enforced against a figure somebody actually measured - a substituted nought
hands every assistant its whole ceiling again, every month, for as long as the meter is broken.
An assistant missing from aiEvaluations has NEVER BEEN CHECKED for accuracy, which
the screen says in those words rather than showing a score of nought.
